limitations: Five dictated utterances, one speaker, one session. That is enough to show an effect is real and to characterise its spread. It is not enough to characterise its distribution, and no confidence interval is claimed.
The five utterances are technical instructions the author wrote and then read aloud. They are not a random sample of development speech, and the results should not be read as one.
The spoken side is the script, not a transcript. A local ASR engine read the same audio and disagreed with Wispr in both directions, so neither is treated as ground truth.
The scorer does not normalise spoken number words. '99' arriving as 'ninety nine' is counted as a loss even though the meaning is intact, which adds noise to every figure.
Backslash escaping of underscores was not understood during collection and is not modelled. Four identifiers were affected and are reported by inspection instead.
Reading pace was not held constant across the passes.
Audio is not published, because it contains a voice.
